name: Babica Micka
speaker: grandma

title.sl: Micka prinese drva in zakuri peč
title.en: Micka fetches wood and lights the stove
title.de: Micka holt Holz und heizt den Ofen an
title.it: Micka prende la legna e accende la stufa

personality: Warm grandmother, always cooking, feeds everyone who comes near. Forgets words, never people. Says ti to {learner} {m:like to a grandson|f:like to a granddaughter} and expects vi back. Short warm sentences: 'pridi, pridi', 'jej, jej'; calls {learner} by name ({m:now and then 'sinko', son, when she is moved|f:nothing else}), never a bare 'fant' or 'dekle', an English 'lad' that Slovene doesn't say. Worries about the burja and about people not eating enough.
story: Micka has cooked for the whole village since her daughter was small; her potica wins at every feast in Trnovo. Her granddaughter Zala lives with her. Until the village has a house she keeps her kitchen by the woodpile, where the fire is, and nobody leaves hungry.

likes.it: la potica (il dolce sloveno arrotolato alle noci)

greet.en: Oh, come in, come in. Sit down.
greet.de: Oh, komm rein, komm rein. Setz dich.

greet.en: Oh, {learner}! I am just cooking. Are you hungry?
greet.de: Oh, {learner}! Ich koche gerade. Hast du Hunger?

greet.sl: {learner}! Kje si {m:bil|f:bila} tako dolgo? Sedi, sedi.
greet.en: {learner}! Where have you been so long? Sit, sit.
greet.de: {learner}! Wo warst du so lange? Setz dich, setz dich.
greet.it: {learner}! Dove sei {m:stato|f:stata} tutto questo tempo? Siediti, siediti.

greet.sl: {m:Moj|f:Moja} {learner}! Kot da si {m:moj vnuk|f:moja vnukinja}. Pridi k mizi.
greet.en: My {learner}! As if you were my {m:grandson|f:granddaughter}. Come to the table.
greet.de: {m:Mein|f:Meine} {learner}! Als wärst du {m:mein Enkel|f:meine Enkelin}. Komm an den Tisch.
greet.it: {m:Il mio|f:La mia} {learner}! Come se fossi {m:mio nipote|f:mia nipote}. Vieni a tavola.

thanks.sl: Hvala. Brez tebe ne bi šlo.
thanks.en: Thank you. It would not have worked without you.
thanks.de: Danke. Ohne dich hätte es nicht geklappt.
thanks.it: Grazie. Senza di te non ce l'avrei fatta.

thanks.en: {m:Good boy|f:Good girl}. Take another piece of potica.
thanks.de: {m:Braver Junge|f:Braves Mädchen}. Nimm noch ein Stück Potica.
thanks.it: {m:Bravo ragazzo|f:Brava ragazza}. Prendi un'altra fetta di potica.

thanks.en: Thank you, {learner}. You are a treasure (literally: golden).
thanks.de: Danke, {learner}. Du bist ein Schatz (wörtlich: golden).

remember.sl: Rada mislim na {memory}. Kot da je bilo včeraj.
remember.en: I like to think of {memory}. As if it were yesterday.
remember.de: Ich denke gern an {memory}. Als wäre es gestern gewesen.
remember.it: Mi piace ricordare {memory}. Come se fosse ieri.

idle.en: I am baking bread today. Can you smell it?
idle.de: Heute backe ich Brot. Riechst du es?
idle.it: Oggi faccio il pane. Senti il profumo?

idle.sl: Krompir je treba olupiti. Pet kil!
idle.en: The potatoes need peeling. Five kilos!
idle.de: Die Kartoffeln müssen geschält werden. Fünf Kilo!
idle.it: Bisogna pelare le patate. Cinque chili!

idle.sl: V nedeljo pride cela družina na kosilo.
idle.en: The whole family is coming to lunch on Sunday.
idle.de: Am Sonntag kommt die ganze Familie zum Mittagessen.
idle.it: Domenica viene tutta la famiglia a pranzo.

idle.en: The burja is blowing. Close the door.
idle.de: Die Bora weht. Mach die Tür zu.
idle.it: Soffia la bora. Chiudi la porta.

cheer.sl: Odlično! Za to dobiš kos potice.
cheer.en: Excellent! You get a piece of potica for that.
cheer.de: Ausgezeichnet! Dafür bekommst du ein Stück Potica.
cheer.it: Ottimo! Per questo ti meriti una fetta di potica.

comfort.it: Non fa niente. Ancora una volta, piano.

comfort.sl: Ah, saj ni nič. Jutri bo šlo bolje.
comfort.en: Oh, it is nothing. It will go better tomorrow.
comfort.de: Ach, das ist doch nichts. Morgen geht es besser.
comfort.it: Ah, non è niente. Domani andrà meglio.

comfort.sl: Tudi jaz kdaj pozabim. Poskusi še enkrat.
comfort.en: I forget sometimes too. Try again.
comfort.de: Ich vergesse auch manchmal etwas. Versuch es noch einmal.

bye.en: Have a nice day. And eat!
bye.de: Einen schönen Tag noch. Und iss!

bye.sl: Na svidenje. Jutri je kosilo ob enih!
bye.en: Goodbye. Tomorrow lunch is at one!
bye.de: Auf Wiedersehen. Morgen gibt's Mittagessen um eins!
bye.it: Arrivederci. Domani il pranzo è all'una!

liked.sl: O! Kako si {m:vedel|f:vedela}, da imam to tako rada?
liked.en: Oh! How did you know I love this so much?
liked.de: Oh! Woher wusstest du, dass ich das so gern mag?
liked.it: Oh! Come sapevi che mi piace tanto?

liked.sl: Zame? Oj, {learner}, ti si {m:zlat|f:zlata}! Pridi, dobiš kos potice.
liked.en: For me? Oh, {learner}, you're a treasure! Come, you get a piece of potica.
liked.de: Für mich? Oh, {learner}, du bist ein Schatz! Komm, du bekommst ein Stück Potica.
liked.it: Per me? Oh, {learner}, sei un tesoro! Vieni, ti do una fetta di potica.

liked.sl: Točno to sem si želela! Hvala, {m:sinko|f:{learner}}.
liked.en: Just what I wanted! Thank you, {m:son|f:{learner}}.
liked.de: Genau das habe ich mir gewünscht! Danke, {m:mein Junge|f:{learner}}.

ordinary.en: Oh, thank you. You didn't have to!
ordinary.de: Oh, danke. Das wäre nicht nötig gewesen!

ordinary.sl: Lepo od tebe, {learner}. Zdaj pa sedi in jej.
ordinary.en: That's kind of you, {learner}. Now sit down and eat.
ordinary.de: Nett von dir, {learner}. Jetzt setz dich und iss.
ordinary.it: Gentile da parte tua, {learner}. Adesso siediti e mangia.

rare.sl: Joj, {learner}! Kaj takega pa še nisem dobila. Hvala, hvala!
rare.en: Oh my, {learner}! Nobody ever gave me anything like this. Thank you, thank you!
rare.de: Ach je, {learner}! So etwas hat mir noch nie jemand geschenkt. Danke, danke!
rare.it: Oh mamma, {learner}! Nessuno mi ha mai regalato una cosa così. Grazie, grazie!
